latest_release.name: v5.0.1
latest_release.body:
- rust-anything is now dual licensed under MIT OR Apache-2.0, the usual license for Rust projects. You
  can keep using it under MIT exactly as before; Apache-2.0 adds an explicit patent grant. `LICENSE` is
  now `LICENSE-MIT`, next to a new `LICENSE-APACHE`, and both ship in the crate, the npm package and
  the release archives.
- `map` counts units, not crates, in its first line: one unit bridged twice (napi and wasm, or a
  second `bridge --out`) reads `1 of 1 unit has a Rust port` instead of `2 of 2 units have`. The
  Ports table still lists every crate (#609 by @Aadithya-kl).
- `fuzz --time` given a negative or non-finite value says
  `` `--time` must be 0 or more seconds (0 runs one round), not -1 `` instead of
  `` `--time` takes seconds ``, and `--time -1` (with a space) gets the same message instead of clap's
  `unexpected argument '-1' found`. The MCP `fuzz` tool's `time` says the same (#612).
- `bridge --as-json Q` stops before writing anything when no export declares `Q` as a type
  parameter, with ``--as-json `Q` is not a type parameter of `src/math.ts` (type parameters: T)``
  (or "it has none"), instead of ignoring the name and leaving the generic export in TS, as
  `--keep` already does for unknown exports (#608).

detail.readme:
Rust Anything


Migrate your app to Rust, and prove it still behaves the same.

Documentation: https://rustanything.ai/

🌐 Other languages

Moving a codebase to Rust? I offer consulting for Rust migrations: hello@rustanything.ai

## Sponsors

Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by erKam Yaman
Rust Anything is free and open source. If it helps your work, sponsoring keeps it going.

Your safety comes first: sponsors get a logo and a link here, nothing more. No paid recommendations and no setup guides for third-party AI API resellers, so nothing here steers your code, keys or data somewhere you didn't choose.

Sponsoring as a company, or anything else? hello@rustanything.ai

Moving a codebase to Rust? I offer consulting for Rust migrations: hello@rustanything.ai

## Quick start Paste this into your coding agent: ```text Install Rust Anything with npm i -g rust-anything, then run rust-anything setup. Run rust-anything go -- and finish the port until rust-anything gate passes. ``` Or install it yourself: ```sh cargo install rust-anything # or: npm install -g rust-anything rust-anything setup # adds it to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode ``` > [!TIP] > **Agents:** read [rustanything.ai/llms.txt](https://rustanything.ai/llms.txt) for the install steps, every command and the porting workflow. ## How it works

**What counts as done.** Behavior, not your tests. `record` runs the original on generated and given inputs and saves what each call returns, throws and prints. A port is done when `gate` passes: every recorded case matches, and fmt, clippy, `cargo test`, the `unsafe` check, the stub check and the check for recorded answers pasted into the port all pass. Your own tests run too. **Report or migrate, you pick.** `analyze` and `profile` only report: a ranked plan of what to port, and what is hot under a real workload. They are plain commands, so the report costs no tokens. `go` migrates one unit: it bridges the hottest function, records it, hands the port to your agent, then builds, diffs and gates it, and switches it on only when everything matches (TS/JS, Python and PowerShell; `disable` switches it back off). **How long a run takes.** One `go` run ports one unit, with at most `--rounds` agent turns (3 by default): one for the port, then one per failing diff or gate. A whole app is one run per unit, so you can stop after any of them. **Cheap model for the plan, strong model for the port.** The plan needs no model. For the port, pass any agent command: `rust-anything go --agent "claude --model " -- `. **Agents.** `rust-anything setup` adds it to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode. Any other MCP client can run `rust-anything mcp`, and the skill also installs on its own with `npx skills add erkamyaman/rust-anything` (see [install](docs/install.md)). ## License Licensed under either of [MIT](./LICENSE-MIT) or [Apache-2.0](./LICENSE-APACHE), at your option. © [Erkam Yaman](https://github.com/erkamyaman). Ports and generated code in your repository are yours. Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution you intentionally submit for inclusion in rust-anything, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, is dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.
